description:
The enumerated-anchor mechanism that makes a fabricated anchor impossible exists in this file and is wired only to the path the failures do not take. Extending it to the primary drafting path is the single highest-leverage change available to the authoring lane.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS. In the re-derivation block, feature-compose.ts offers the model a numbered list of verified-unique anchors and takes the bytes from OUR list rather than from the model's output. Its own comment states the principle: "let it pick an INDEX and take the bytes from the verified list here. The anchor then CANNOT be invented, because the model never writes it." That block also handles the details correctly — an indexed answer wins over free text, the window-provenance check is deliberately skipped for an indexed anchor because such an anchor has better provenance than the window test, a single-candidate list is auto-accepted, and every check fails open.

WHERE IT IS NOT. The identifier `anchor_index` occurs at exactly four lines in this file, ALL inside that re-derivation block. The PRIMARY drafting path still asks the model to reproduce an anchor as text: it logs "[fc-anchors] supplied verified-unique anchors for <path> (N locator candidate(s))" and then requests a verbatim old_string. The drafter demonstrably paraphrases what it is shown — measured on src/seed/index.ts, an untouched file: the source has `export const SEED_TEMPLATES: ActivityTemplate[] = [` and the model returned it without the type annotation; the source has `export { X } from "./add-resolver-to-vessel.js";` and the model returned it without the from-clause. Indentation is altered the same way.

PROMPT-LEVEL CORRECTION HAS BEEN TRIED AND DOES NOT WORK ON THIS CLASS. Commit 12c4c58 added an explicit instruction not to return the failed anchor, and the very next repair echoed it anyway. The re-derivation comment reaches the same conclusion independently: "A model that ignores a list will ignore a longer one, so stop asking it to reproduce a string at all." The lever must be mechanical.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING. Hard anchor failure (apply_failed with ops_applied == 0) accounts for roughly 28% of compose attempts, and the composer's own rate has sat at 20-23% since 2026-09-08 against a 10-12% baseline on 09-05/06. This is the dominant loss in the authoring lane.

SHAPE OF THE CHANGE. Two sites must move together, which is why it has not happened incrementally: the drafting prompt must render the verified-unique anchors as an INDEXED list with an instruction to answer with an index, and the plan-application path must resolve an op's anchor_index against that same list before falling back to op.old_string. Both halves must be in one change; a prompt that offers indices to an applier that ignores them is worse than neither, because the model will spend its answer on a field that is dropped.

DO NOT THREAD THE LIST THROUGH FUNCTION SIGNATURES. Two prior attempts on this file died on cross-scope bindings (TS2339, TS2304) and one on changing a return type without changing its declaration (TS2322: returning {text, conceptIds} from a function still declared Promise<string>). Use a module-scoped array holding the last rendered anchor list for the file being planned, written where the list is built and read where the op is applied. Anchor every edit on a single short line; measured landing on this file collapses as anchor length grows.

FAIL OPEN, AND CHANGE NOTHING ELSE. An absent, non-numeric or out-of-range index must fall through to today's exact behaviour, so the change can only add a path and never remove one. Preserve the existing uniqueness check and refuseRederivedEdit call unchanged.

VERIFY BEHAVIOURALLY. The claim is not that the code contains a new identifier. It is that the hard anchor-failure rate falls. compose-drift-tick already measures exactly this population (apply_failed AND ops_applied == 0 over feature_compose executions, day-scale) against the composer's own median baseline, so the closure test is a sustained fall in that rate on complete days after the change lands, with the day the change landed recorded. Note this file has NO TEST FILE, so every gate reads the diff and none executes it; a FAVORABLE verdict here means reviewed, not run.
